units: <cite ref="Taanit 12b:10">Taan. 12ᵇ</cite> <he>יחיד … ת׳</he> an individual that vowed to fast.
<cite ref="Taanit 12b:10">Ib.</cite> <he>ת׳ יחיד</he> a private fast-day; <he>ת׳ ציבור</he> public fast.
<cite ref="Taanit 12b:10">Ib.</cite> <he>שמא ת׳ ציבור קבל עליו</he> may-be he vowed a fast with the restrictions of a public fast.
<cite ref="Taanit 12b:10">Ib.</cite> <he>לווה אדם תַּעֲנִיתוֹ ופורע</he> one may borrow his fast and pay it, i.e. one may break his private fast, and make up for it on another day.
<cite ref="Taanit 12b:10">Ib.</cite> <he>ת׳ חלום</he> a fast on account of a bad dream.
<cite ref="Taanit 12b:10">Ib.</cite>; <cite ref="Shabbat 11a:7">Sabb. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>יפה ת׳ לחלום וכ׳</he> fasting is as good to avert a bad dream as fire to consume flax.
<cite ref="Taanit 11a:14">Taan. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>היושב בת׳ נקרא חוטא</he> he that fasts for self-affliction is called a sinner; a. v. fr.—Pl. <he>תַּעֲנִיּוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Taanit 1:4">Ib. I, 4</cite> <he>הגיע … מתענין שלשה ת׳</he> when the seventeenth day of Marḥeshvan comes, and no rain has fallen, the select begin to observe three fast-days.
Ib. 5 בית דין … ת׳ the court decrees three fast-days; a. fr.—Taʿănith, Taʿăniyoth, name of a treatise, of the Order of Moʿed, of Mishnah, Tosefta, Talmud Babli and Y’rushalmi.
